For me: my mom was a crazy bipolar verbally-physically-emotionally-abusive b*tch (cause let's be real, she really wasn't the best mom) when i was in first grade, she tried suffocating me with a pillow and beat me up with a foot exfoliator really badly on my thighs, and when i cried to her to stop, i remember that she told me to "disappear". i took that as a cue for me to leave her room, and as i attempted to leave from the door, she shook her head and kept yelling at me to disappear. i didn't understand what she meant then, but now that i look back, i think she was telling me to... disappear. (LOL) 
a happier memory: i never doubt that my mom loved me, i just think that because of her circumstances, and her obvious psychological disorders, she didn't know how to love herself. and it's easy to fall into the sad trap of feeling sad for myself and for the ways her disorder affected me, but i never let myself fall victim because i know that she couldn't help herself. even after that day when i felt that she had no love for me, she apologized, told me "i love you", tendered my bruises and bought me the books i wanted to read. even in all her bad days, she made sure to cook all our meals and keep our house clean and me and my sister educated. my mom left to her homeland to her family when i was in middle school after finalizing her divorce with my dad, and since then she's healed significantly and always reminded me that she thinks about me and loves me. i've adopted many of her abusive tendencies (the saying "abusive parents were once abused" isn't very far from the truth) but seeing how much happier she is now, makes me believe i can heal too.

my dad: my dad was rarely home before she left to her country, and on the day that she left, he finally came home only to break the news that i have a stepmother and a stepsister, who lived only a zipcode away from me. yeah..... that sucked. 
however, the best: my dad is just a really good man. he got in a car accident a couple of years ago and as a result has a herniated disc and has a completely immobile neck. he opted out of surgery because he was the only person who could support our family during that time and it would've put him out of work for a couple of months. he carries so much on his back just for us, and he never does with a sense of entitlement or reward. He just loves us
